title: Blending and Segmenting Sounds
introduction: Practise blending and segmenting sounds with familiar words and short sentences.
definition: Blending joins sounds to read a word. Segmenting separates a word into sounds to help spell it.
rules: Blend short words with different vowels before moving to consonant clusters.
Say each sound without adding an extra vowel. In flag, hear f, l, the short a sound and g.
Say stop slowly: /s/ /t/ /o/ /p/. Each sound matters.

examples.question: Blend d-r-u-m.
steps: Join d and r, then u and m.

examples.question: Blend s-w-i-m.
steps: Keep the initial s and w sounds.

examples.question: Blend g-r-e-e-n.
steps: The letters ee represent one long vowel sound.

exercises.question: Join b-l-o-c-k.
exercises.solution: Blend the bl sound, short o and final ck sound.

exercises.question: Join f-r-o-g.
exercises.solution: Blend fr, short o and final g.

exercises.question: Join s-k-i-p.
exercises.solution: Blend sk, short i and final p.

exercises.question: Join s-t-a-r.
exercises.solution: Blend st with the ar sound.

exercises.question: Join t-r-i-p.
exercises.solution: Blend tr, short i and final p.

exercises.question: Join s-n-a-p.
exercises.solution: Blend sn, short a and final p.

exercises.question: Join b-r-u-s-h.
exercises.solution: Blend br, short u and the sh sound.

exercises.question: Join g-r-a-s-s.
exercises.solution: Blend gr, the vowel sound and final ss sound.

exercises.question: Write the first two letters in clap.
exercises.solution: Look at the first two letters before the a.

exercises.question: Write the final two letters in desk.
exercises.solution: Look at the two letters after de.

summary: Blending joins sounds to read a word. Segmenting separates a word into sounds to help spell it.
